newsitem.title: USA: Polymer says to bid for Merfin.
newsitem.headline: Polymer says to bid for Merfin.

text.p: Polymer Group Inc said Friday it will offer to buy all outstanding common shares of Merfin International Inc, either directly or through a Canadian subsidiary.

Under the Polymer offer, a Merfin common shareholder may elect to receive a cash payment of C$7.15 per Merfin common share, or an average undiscounted price per Merfin common share of no less than C$7.60 and no more than C$8.68.

To implement the second option, Polymer would pay Merfin shareholders an amount equal to C$7.60 per common share, with 55 percent in cash upon the closing of the purchase. The remaining 45 percent would be paid with a non-interest bearing promissory note entitling shareholders to receive, on May 31, 1999, a minimum C$7.60 and maximum C$10 per common share, Polymer said.
The actual amount would be based on Merfin's fiscal 1998 earnings, before income taxes, depreciation and amortization, measured against Merfin management's target for the period.
Polymer said its offer will not be conditional on the support of the Merfin board of directors. It said its offer will be mailed to Merfin shareholders as soon as practical.
